svg.title: The four write destinations, and how long each one lasts
svg.desc: A hand-drawn figure with four destination cards across the top. A memory store holds facts about a subject that outlive the session, lasting months and decaying in confidence. A scratchpad holds this task's working notes between tool calls, lasting one task. Repository documents hold rules and stable knowledge in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, reviewed in pull requests and lasting until the policy or build changes. An embedding index holds the corpus itself, chunked offline, lasting until the source changes. A band beneath states the governing rule: every write carries metadata — who wrote it, when, from what source, with what confidence. Two dashed boxes mark what is never written: transient data such as tool results and conversation turns, and secrets such as tokens and keys.
svg.text: Four places to write, and how long each one lasts
Writing is mechanically the easy operation. The hardness is governance: anything written becomes data a future call will trust.
Every write carries metadata: who wrote it, when, from what source, with what confidence.
A tool result is not a memory. A conversation turn is not a memory.
Tokens and keys do not enter a writable store, at any lifetime.
A memory entry with no provenance is indistinguishable from a poisoned one.
